newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Splinter group attacks former party allies-paper.
newsitem.headline: Splinter group attacks former party allies-paper.

text.p: Five people were injured when members of a newly formed political group in Morocco broke into an office of their former local party, the al-Bayane daily said on Monday.
As many as 14 members armed with knives and wooden sticks were involved in the attack, the newspaper said.
The paper is the mouthpiece of the opposition Socialism and Progress Party (SPP) which said the attack took place on Sunday in the northern town of Nador.

"Some 14 people including three unidentified persons broke into (the SPP) headquarters with knives and sticks and started beating up the members present, injuring four militants and the mother of one of them," al-Bayane said.
The men removed the party name plate and took documents and some pieces of furniture, the newspaper added, without explaining any motive for the raid.
A splinter group broke away from the SPP last month, calling itself the Front of Democratic Forces.

The official news agency MAP quoted the group as saying then: "Our target is to renovate the political action (in Morocco), lay down a structure of democratic rules inside the party before a nation-wide struggle for real democratic institutions."
Morocco has a dozen political parties, of which five opposition groups are also represented in the 333-seat parliament, including SPP headed by the 70-year-old veteran politician Ali Yata.
